obligations.text: For the same definition, descriptors, calibrations, sources, execution policy, extraction programs and prompt templates, `rustev plan compile`, the Node binding's `compile` and `command('compile')`, and `rustev_core::compile_with_extraction_documents` produce byte-identical plans with the same `PlanId`.

A call that supplies no extraction program and no prompt template calls the same core function as before this spec, so every existing plan, `PlanId`, CLI golden, conformance case and binding result keeps its bytes.

A compile refusal for a definition compiled with extraction programs or prompt templates carries the core's category and category name on every surface; no surface adds, renames, reorders or swallows a core refusal.
No contract type, JSON Schema or generated binding type changes; `rustev-core` and `rustev-contract` take no new dependency; the WebAssembly package's surface is unchanged.

sectionHeadings: 073: Extraction programs and prompt templates on the CLI's and the Node binding's compile (amends 006, 027 and 063)
record.summary: A proposed amendment of approved specs 006 (3.4), 027 (3.3, 3.12) and 063 (3.2), for #598, targeting release 0.8.0. `rustev-core` compiles a definition with supplied `rustev.extract-rules/1` and `/2` programs and `rustev.prompt-template/1` documents through `compile_with_extraction_documents`, but no host surface reaches it: the Node binding's `compile` takes descriptors, calibrations, sources and an execution policy only, and the CLI's `--rules` takes a rules backend program (spec 005), not an extraction program. A host that keeps its definitions and extraction programs in its own repository can therefore run a `fill: rules_first` plan from Node but cannot build one. This spec adds two optional, repeatable inputs, extraction programs and prompt templates, to `rustev plan check` and `rustev plan compile` (the flags `--extract-rules` and `--template`), to the Node binding's `compile`/`compileSync` option bag (`extractRules`, `templates`) and to its `command('check' | 'compile')`, each routed through `compile_with_extraction_documents`. Compile refusals keep the core's category codes on every surface, and a malformed document is refused as each surface already refuses a malformed descriptor. A call that supplies neither input calls what it calls today, so every existing plan, `PlanId`, golden and output keeps its bytes. No contract type, JSON Schema or generated binding type changes.
